newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines raises oil prices by avg 79.75 centavo.
newsitem.headline: Philippines raises oil prices by avg 79.75 centavo.

text.p: The Energy Regulatory Board (ERB) announced on Tuesday it will raise prices of petroleum products by an average of 79.75 centavos per litre.
The price adjustments will take effect on December 4 at 6 a.m. (2200 GMT December 3).
However, the whole burden of the oil price hike will not be passed on to consumers as some of it will be borne by the Oil Price Stabilisation Fund (OPSF), a government-run buffer fund.

The buffer fund, a relic from the days when the Philippine oil industry was totally regulated, is now labouring under a huge deficit and it is meant to be dissolved once full deregulation takes place in March next year.
To soften the impact of the transition to market-determined prices, the government had decided to restrict monthly hikes in any petroleum product prices to a maximum of 50 centavos per litre.
The latest hike will therefore affect consumers only up to a maximum of 50 centavos while the excess amount will be borne by the OPSF.
Faylona said prices of premium, unleaded and regular gasoline along with fuel oil, diesel oil, liquefied petroleum gasoline and aviation turbo will increase by 50 centavos per litre.
Kerosene prices will be raised by 32 centavos while price of aviation turbo will be raised by 32.11 centavos.

"This price build-up represents two items, one is the regular increase based on the Singapore Posted Prices and under-recovery because of the delay in the oil price adjustment last November 15," Faylona said.

The ERB is required to adjust petroleum prices monthly based on Singapore oil prices but the board decided to suspend last month's adjustment upon complaints of members of the Congress that the previous adjustments were unwarranted.
The oil price increase will be the highest since an automatic oil price formula was implemented in August this year as part of the oil industry deregulation.
